# Profile results automation

The refresh workflow lives in **[rig-c/.github](https://github.com/rig-c/.github)**,
where it runs daily and on `workflow_dispatch`. This repository supplies the two
table generators and `tools/profile_results.py`; it does not publish to the
profile on results pushes. The profile workflow checks out public exam `main`,
records the actual exam checkout SHA, and updates its own `profile/README.md`
through one fixed-branch PR. Review and merge remain a human sign.

The workflow uses only its repository's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` with
`contents: write` and `pull-requests: write`; **no additional secrets are needed**.
Polling means a results change can wait up to a day for the next scheduled run,
plus any GitHub scheduler delay. A manual dispatch can refresh sooner. Checks on
`GITHUB_TOKEN`-created PRs do not run automatically; the signer must run or approve
the appropriate checks before merging. The destination workflow's README explains
dispatch setup and the first-run default-branch requirement.

## Generated regions and migration

`tools/profile_results.py` writes the **exact stdout bytes**, including the final
newline, of:

```sh
python3 results.py --profile
python3 advanced/results.py --profile
```

These replace the bodies of `exam:start` / `exam:end` and `exam-advanced:start` /
`exam-advanced:end`. The existing marker comments are preserved. A third pair,
`exam-summary:start` / `exam-summary:end`, owns just two derived count paragraphs.
All markers must be complete HTML comments on their own lines, with exactly one
ordered, non-overlapping pair per region. A missing table marker, a partial or
duplicate summary pair, or overlapping regions fails before writing the file.

The first run supports the two-pair profile before and after `rig-c/.github#5`:
the Basic sentence beginning **“Every line passed, and the three models named…”**
or **“Eleven models have sat it, from each vendor's lighter tier…”**, and the
Advanced sentence beginning **“Five/Six models have sat all three rounds and one
cell failed…”** through **“(shown here as a what-if).”** These exact sentence
templates allow changed numeric counts and line wrapping. Only those obsolete
sentences are removed. The invitation to sit the exam, Advanced's introduction,
links and unrelated prose remain. The summary pair is inserted immediately after
the Basic table. A second run is a byte no-op and does not rewrite the file.

If an editor has changed those sentences into an unrecognised form, the workflow
refuses to guess. In a reviewed profile change, remove **only** the stale count or
result-comparison sentences, preserve the other prose, and insert this empty pair
outside the two table regions. Then rerun the workflow to populate it:

```html
<!-- exam-summary:start — generated by rig-c/exam; do not edit by hand -->
<!-- exam-summary:end -->
```

The summary reads the existing generators' data and selection functions; it does
not change tables or grade any run:

- **Basic:** group by the same directory/model key, include only `counted()`
  sittings (`counts` starts with `independent`), and count a model as passing every
  graded line only if it has graded tasks and every task in every counted sitting
  has a positive denominator and `passed == of`. This includes tasks on Round 5's
  separately tabled painting. Missing tasks do not establish a pass or completion
  of the whole exam. Repeated sittings do not add models.
- **Advanced:** use `by_model(sittings())`, including its last-sitting-per-round
  selection and without adding an independence filter. A model passes all three
  only with R1, R2 and R3 present and every selected grade having a positive
  denominator, `passed == of`, and all row statuses `PASS`. FAIL and SKIP prevent
  that count. The non-passing cell count covers only selected, present rounds.
  Shin-scale what-ifs never change these counts; a native edition's shin row is
  already part of its recorded grade.

## Local targeted verification

No Node install, grader, build or full exam suite is needed. Set `TMPDIR` to an existing directory
outside all repositories and keep dependencies there as well:

```sh
python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --target "$TMPDIR/profile-pydeps" -r .github/requirements-profile-tests.txt
PYTHONPATH="$TMPDIR/profile-pydeps" python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tools -p 'test_profile_results.py' -v
```

`profile-results-test.yml` runs this targeted suite in CI. The fixture is the
two-pair public profile read for this change. Tests cover the real CLI outputs,
both legacy migrations, preservation, malformed/missing/duplicate markers,
counting edge cases, the local CLI, and its second-run no-op. Tests use
temporary directories under `TMPDIR` and never invoke Git or publish. CI uses the runner's external
temporary directory by default. The profile repository owns
the refresh workflow's contracts and remote checkout/commit/PR verification.
